t: For acquisition of land within the exterior boundaries of the Cache National Forest, Utah; Uinta and Wasatch National Forests, Utah; Toiyabe National Forest, Nevada; Angeles National Forest, California; and, San Bernardino and Cleveland National Forests, California, as authorized by law, $325,000, to be derived from forest receipts.

fable.w: This section only appropriates money, drawn from forest receipts, for acquiring land within named National Forests. It provides for no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. The only possible temptation is that land acquisition affects states or landowners, but the text sets out no process that brings them into a federal decision.
fable.s: as authorized by law, $325,000, to be derived from forest receipts.

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple appropriation clause authorizing the expenditure of funds for land acquisition. It does not mention any process for consulting with outside parties, holding public hearings, or involving non-federal entities in the decision-making process. The phrase 'as authorized by law' refers to existing statutory authority for the agency to acquire land, not to a specific participation requirement within this text.
qwen_block.s: For acquisition of land within the exterior boundaries of the Cache National Forest, Utah; Uinta and Wasatch National Forests, Utah; Toiyabe National Forest, Nevada; Angeles National Forest, California; and, San Bernardino and Cleveland National Forests, California, as authorized by law, $325,000, to be derived from forest receipts.

opus.w: This section only appropriates $325,000, taken from forest receipts, to buy land within named national forests. No outside party (state, tribe, public, expert, or company) is consulted, given a hearing, or given a right to challenge the decision. Like Example 1, it is a plain funding provision with no process for outsiders to take part.
opus.b: This is an appropriation for buying land inside several national forests. A reader might be tempted to call it participation because acquiring land "as authorized by law" sounds like a formal decision process. But nothing in the text brings in anyone outside the federal government. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue.
